review.notes:
Chain starts at v4 (LCYW-EN178, 2012-09-29), where text_matches_version points. The pre-errata cdb string ('Once per turn, during your Standby Phase, pay 700 LP or destroy this card') matches no lineage version verbatim (0.837) - it is upstream's modern-wording rendering of v4's 'During each of your Standby Phases, pay 700 Life Points or destroy this card', semantically identical since you have exactly one Standby Phase per turn, and the script's SetCountLimit(1) is present in both variants. Earlier transitions predate the baseline and are not recorded: v0 -> v1 is Magic -> Spell, and v1 -> v2 (DB1-EN086, 2004-10-12) changes 'If you cannot, this card is destroyed' to 'If you do not', which reads as making the payment optional - potentially behavioural, but it sits before the version the baseline implements and is not evaluated here. The remaining script differences are equivalent modernisations of the negation check (s.distarget/s.disoperation renamed, tl==LOCATION_SZONE for a bitmask test, re:IsActiveType(TYPE_SPELL) for re:IsSpellEffect()), matching the cosmetic 'Spell Card effects' -> 'Spell effects' wording, and are not recorded as a change.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Imperial Order). The rulings read support d2 at both snapshots (the passages are in the check); nothing contradicts a claimed difference, so kind, summary and coverage are unchanged. Verdicts: [event] d1 unresolved at Edison, unresolved at Tengu; d2 supported at Edison, supported at Tengu.

effective.basis: TCG release of the first printing carrying the errata'd text (DUSA-EN049, Duelist Saga) Independently corroborated by Konami's own errata announcement and the archived Forbidden & Limited List page carrying its effective date; the printing remains the anchor because it is when the text first became available in the TCG (the announcement and the F/L effective date differ by a few days).

event.historical_text: Negate all Spell Card effects on the field. During each of your Standby Phases, pay 700 Life Points or destroy this card.
event.modern_text: Negate all Spell effects on the field. Once per turn, during the Standby Phase, you must pay 700 LP (this is not optional), or this card is destroyed.
event.summary: Functional erratum with two mechanisms. The maintenance cost moved from your own Standby Phase to every Standby Phase: the pre-errata script gates the effect on s.mtcon returning Duel.GetTurnPlayer()==tp, which the modern script drops, matching 'During each of your Standby Phases' becoming 'Once per turn, during the Standby Phase'. The payment also became mandatory: the pre-errata script wraps it in Duel.SelectYesNo so the controller may decline and let Imperial Order be destroyed, while the modern script pays whenever Duel.CheckLPCost succeeds, matching 'you must pay 700 LP (this is not optional)'.

rulings_check.difference: Era: the maintenance cost applies only during its controller's own Standby Phase ('During each of your Standby Phases'); modern: it applies in every Standby Phase, including the opponent's ('Once per turn, during the Standby Phase'). Era: paying the 700 Life Points is a choice, and the controller may decline and let Imperial Order be destroyed even with enough Life Points; modern: the payment is mandatory (the card is destroyed only if the cost cannot be paid).
